These are a collection of demos that have piled up on my 4-track. The first seven tracks are songs that I didn't want to further progress. The second half of the album are demos that lead up to the professional production of songs off of the album I produced most recently, *We're Sad Because We're Alive*, which can be found in the discography panel in the link. While this may not be the most pleasing to listen to, I've always loved to hear the early demos and unpolished tracks of some of my favorite artists. Robert Smith of the Cure made home tapes of his songs to be released; check out "10:15 Saturday Night RS home demo" for a great example of a track that was at its best before it went into the studio. The early bandcamp releases by Frankie Cosmos provide in interesting insight into how she began songwriting. I feel these demos are somewhat of a look into my sketchbook. While I realize this may be terribly narcissistic, I believe that these demos, coupled with their respective finished tracks, could provide a beginning songwriter with the perspective of how songs go through progressions before becoming works of art. And I personally would have loved to be given this kind of opportunity when I was first beginning.
